scope: A dated discovery and compatibility snapshot, not a live version authority. Check each repository and release for newer evidence. The four releases recorded here were read from their GitHub Release pages, including each asset's published SHA-256.

coordination.work_tracking: The existing Linear WuwaTerm project remains authoritative for work tracking.

api.note: API v1 alone does not establish review-v2 or private Web auth-status capability.

features.note: Both features are additive on review-v2 only. dense-128 raises the finding page from 32 to 128 and stays bounded by the 64 KiB body ceiling Core 0.10.0 serves, and reason-v1 adds a reason to each not_evaluated finding. A request without the header answers the published 32-finding, seven-key document; a header on review-v1, an unknown or repeated token, or an empty part is invalid_request, and a response that enabled a feature echoes the accepted set in the same header.

manuscript.note: v1 and v2 keep their meaning, and an imported v1 or v2 report, a document-mode choice or a semantic decision stays history, not a fresh check. v3 adds per-segment term results for long manuscripts: a saved segment result is reused only when its content hashes, review basis and request inputs all match a live review-v2 basis. v4 keeps v3's 13 top-level keys, the 44 MiB file limit and the canonical bytes, and raises the findings, resolutions and choices limits from 32 to 128 while allowing a reason on a not_evaluated finding; only the label v4 brings those limits, so a v1, v2 or v3 file keeps its 32-item caps and rejects reason. A writer stores the lowest format that holds the content (v1/v2, then v3, then v4). The v4 contract ships in Web 0.4.0 and Windows 0.6.0, not in Web 0.3.1 or Windows 0.5.1, which reject a v4 file; the shipped-release records below keep the format each release was recorded with.

release.note: v0.10.0 is a review and translation release. review-v2 gives every mapped region its own claim and allocation step: when the occurrences a region holds cannot cover the mentions competing for them, it credits none of those mentions instead of whichever one a sweep reaches first, a partial assignment is the largest one rather than the first one found, an inflection never answers a competing official form, a numbering dot no longer ends a sentence where review-v2 pairs them (segmentation-v1 keeps the boundary it publishes), an occurrence enclosed by a longer official form is not a standalone hit unless the source claims that longer term, a lowercase spelling of a capitalized official term is an ordinary word, and a derived name surface asserts no constraint. The CJK matcher basis label moves to wuwaterm-cjk-matcher-v8, so stored resolution contexts and saved v3 segment results carrying -v7 go stale by the existing freshness rule and are re-reviewed. POST /v1/reviews accepts a 64 KiB body instead of 32 KiB, and review-v2 callers may opt into dense-128 and reason-v1 with X-WuwaTerm-Review-Features under an exact grammar that echoes the accepted set back. Regrouping a context-mode answer into the source's paragraphs refuses a crossing paragraph break and a merge-plus-split line layout and keeps the model's own blank lines. Every LLM request byte, term lock and reference list is identical to 0.9.2, and the builder and the terms.db it produces are unchanged, so an install keeps the database it built. The Web and Windows contract pins move to Web v0.4.0 (7cfbc4d5) and Windows v0.6.0 (eaceb8bb), the two consumers of wuwaterm-manuscript-v4; no Core API version or OpenAPI shape changes with the pins. CI run 44599508979 passed on 67e27da, the draft release run 44602177160 built the assets, and the release-triggered run 44602964761 promoted the image tags. v0.9.2 and its assets remain published under previous_release.

previous_release.note: v0.9.2 reports an OpenAI-compatible endpoint that rejects provider-specific reasoning fields as a diagnostic instead of an ordinary HTTP error: an HTTP 400 whose error object carries code unsupported_parameter and param thinking or reasoning_effort gets the detail unsupported_thinking or unsupported_reasoning_effort, the server warning names only that parameter, the two configuration variables and the accepted alternative, and the provider message, the source text and the request URL are never copied into it. The failed request is still one POST, with no retry, no field removal and no inference from a model name, and the user-facing unavailable notice and the HTTP 503 llm_unavailable envelope are unchanged. Setting WUWATERM_TRANSLATION_THINKING_ZH_EN=omit or WUWATERM_TRANSLATION_THINKING_EN_ZH=omit keeps translating against such an endpoint by sending neither reasoning field. Translation strategy, prompts and the dictionary are unchanged from 0.9.1. Kept as history after v0.10.0; the release and its assets are still published. v0.9.0 and earlier remain on the release page.

Core moves a minor version, so Telegram moves a minor version; the release-prep change (#42) is the Core pin, the package metadata and the docs that describe what Core now does. The code change is #41: a chat's delivering slot is no longer evicted while a report is being delivered and a full slot set answers the busy notice instead, a member who submits the same text while the source job runs is queued by user and served from the finished report without another model call, a send retry is limited to a network error confirmed not to have reached Telegram, the failure notice carries a resend button guarded against double clicks, expired toasts are bilingual, dead job state is removed, and a tag push no longer triggers a second CI run. /review findings follow Core's wuwaterm-cjk-matcher-v8 basis and its numbering-dot rule, and long /tr paragraph regrouping refuses a crossing break and a merge-plus-split layout. Every LLM request byte, term lock and reference list is identical to Core 0.9.2, and the builder and its terms.db are unchanged, so an existing install keeps the database it built. v0.3.1 and its assets remain published under previous_release.

release.note: v0.6.0 reads and writes wuwaterm-manuscript-v4 and adds term grouping and per-occurrence work in the review panel (#30). Findings, resolutions and choices per manuscript or segment rise from 32 to 128, a not_evaluated finding can carry a structured reason, and the review request declares X-WuwaTerm-Review-Features: dense-128,reason-v1; a writer stores the lowest format that holds the content (v1/v2, then v3, then v4), so a manuscript that does not need v4 keeps its lower format and old clients keep opening it. The panel groups the occurrences of one term by form and candidate with a pending filter and reads "another N segments to review" and the not-evaluated reason, per-occurrence replace and revise work in the group, the editor fixes Enter, CRLF and a bare CR concatenation and keeps the caret and selection of a rejected edit, an unreviewed short segment shows as pending again instead of reviewed, and a text that cannot be split reliably after translation gets a jump entry. It requires HTTP API v1, and manuscript review also needs review-v2. Windows 0.5.1 and Web 0.3.1 reject v4 files. v0.5.1 and its assets remain published under previous_release.

compatibility.note: The client reads wuwaterm-manuscript-v1, v2, v3 and v4, and writes the lowest format that holds the content: a v4-only limit (more than 32 findings, resolutions or choices, or a not_evaluated reason) is what moves a file up. Local manuscript editing works offline, and online features require a configured API and device credential.

release.note: v0.4.0 reads and writes wuwaterm-manuscript-v4 and adds term grouping and per-occurrence actions (#45): a dense review (Core feature dense-128) returns up to 128 findings, a not_evaluated finding can carry a reason-v1 reason, and the review panel groups the occurrences of one term by form and candidate with per-occurrence replace and revise, a manual-segmentation banner, a jump helper and segment order and status with the truncation reason. It sends X-WuwaTerm-Review-Features: dense-128,reason-v1 and stays within Core's 64 KiB review body. The release prep (#46) moves the Core and Windows pins to contracts/backend-ref.txt 9a4f680f and contracts/windows-ref.txt eaceb8bb, adds a live-Core contract test that runs the BFF against a Core checkout with and without the feature header and once above 32 KiB, and deletes the v3-only Windows pin so both clients assert the same v4 fixtures. The BFF, the /v1 proxy, the database schema, dependencies and hosting configuration are unchanged since v0.3.1. v0.3.1 and its assets remain published under previous_release.
